summary: Evaluates the Multicast extensions to OSPF (MOSPF) against the criteria the IETF set for routing protocols in RFC 1264. It reports on the protocol's design and on early implementation and deployment experience. It is informational and does not define a standard.

eli5.summary: A teacher grades a new game against a checklist of rules. This paper checks one network delivery method against the list and writes down what worked.

questions: does mospf meet routing protocol criteria
subtitle: Analysis of the multicast routing protocol against IETF standardization criteria.

tldr.problem: MOSPF extends OSPF to route multicast datagrams within an Autonomous System, and the RFC evaluates whether MOSPF meets the IETF's criteria for routing protocol standardization.
tldr.mechanism: MOSPF uses the Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) to discover multicast group members on local networks, floods group membership information via link-state advertisements, and calculates a separate shortest-path tree for each [source, multicast group, TOS] tuple on demand, caching results.
tldr.outcome: Early Proteon implementation shows MOSPF is viable, with modest code size overhead and successful deployment at several sites, though computational scaling and interoperability with other multicast protocols remain open questions.

today: RFC 1585 is an informational document documenting MOSPF's evaluation against IETF routing protocol criteria. It has not been obsoleted. The main MOSPF specification is in RFC 1584.

sections.title: Overview of MOSPF
sections.content:
MOSPF is a multicast routing protocol built as an extension to OSPF. It enables routers within a single Autonomous System to deliver IP multicast datagrams (packets sent to multiple recipients identified by a class D IP address) efficiently. MOSPF monitors multicast group membership using the Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP), which allows hosts to dynamically join and leave multicast groups.

When a MOSPF router detects a host joining a multicast group via IGMP, it floods group membership information throughout the AS using a new type of OSPF link-state advertisement called the group-membership-LSA. MOSPF routers then calculate a separate shortest-path tree for each combination of source network, multicast destination group and IP Type of Service (TOS) on demand, when the first datagram in a stream arrives. These calculations are cached for reuse by later datagrams, reducing computational overhead.
sections.eli5: MOSPF is a way to make OSPF (which normally routes one message to one place) handle messages that go to many places. It learns where each group of listeners is, then figures out the best way to send messages to them.

sections.title: Design Characteristics
sections.content:
MOSPF follows several key design principles. First, source/destination routing means the path of a multicast datagram depends both on its source and its destination group, not just the destination as in standard unicast routing. Second, MOSPF takes advantage of commonality in paths: when members of a group are spread across multiple networks, the datagram is replicated at tree branches, minimizing duplication.

Third, all routers calculate identical shortest-path trees for a given datagram because the tree is rooted at the datagram source (not the calculating router, as in unicast). This ensures a single path between source and any group member. Fourth, MOSPF conforms to link-layer encapsulation standards for IP multicast, using explicit IP-to-datalink multicast address mapping on Ethernet and FDDI.

MOSPF also supports optional TOS-based multicast routing alongside source/destination routing, allows mixing of MOSPF and non-multicast OSPF routers, and provides mechanisms for routing multicast datagrams between OSPF areas and across AS boundaries.
sections.eli5: MOSPF finds the shortest path from the sender to each listener, using as much shared path as possible to avoid sending the same message multiple times. All routers agree on which path to use.

sections.title: Computational Cost and Scaling
sections.content:
MOSPF's main computational challenge is the number of Dijkstra shortest-path calculations. Each [source network, multicast destination, TOS] tuple requires a Dijkstra run, which costs O(N*log(N)) where N is the number of transit nodes. On-demand calculation spreads this cost over time and reduces the work each router must do.

The RFC provides a practical example: in a 200-router OSPF area where each router participates in simultaneous video conferences with three local sites, there are 50 multicast groups and 200 datagram trees. If all calculations happen at once, it would take 3 seconds on a 10 MIPS processor to compute all 200 Dijkstras. However, since video streams consume far more bandwidth than the routing calculations, the routing overhead is manageable. The RFC also notes that by limiting OSPF areas to 200 nodes (per OSPF guidelines), Dijkstra cost is capped; unbounded growth comes from the number of distinct [source, destination] combinations, which is bounded by the number of group members and external sources in the domain.
sections.eli5: MOSPF has to do a lot of math to figure out where to send messages. But it only does the math once per combination of sender and group, and caches the answer. For typical networks, this is not too slow.

sections.title: Implementation Experience
sections.content:
By March 1994, Proteon Inc. had released a full MOSPF implementation (with the exception of TOS-based routing). The implementation was running at approximately a dozen sites, each with 10-20 routers. Proteon added multicast applications including a multicast pinger, console commands to join and leave groups, and the ability to send SNMP traps to a multicast address. The company also used MOSPF to tunnel other protocols such as source route bridging over IP.

Code size comparison shows MOSPF added about 30 percent to the base OSPF implementation. The Proteon implementation includes lines of C code for configuration and monitoring, as well as IGMP. Testing covered topology changes, path verification after cost changes, multicast routing between areas and across AS boundaries, tiebreaker algorithms, NBMA network support and interoperability of MOSPF and non-multicast OSPF routers.

Not yet tested were the interaction between MOSPF and OSPF virtual links, interaction with other multicast routing protocols like DVMRP, and TOS-based multicast routing. Deployment has also been constrained by the lack of a single implementation supporting both MOSPF and DVMRP, which would be needed for Autonomous Systems to connect to the wider multicast backbone (MBONE).
sections.eli5: Engineers at Proteon built and tested MOSPF, and it works. The code is about 30 percent bigger than OSPF. People are using it to send video and other data to multiple sites.

sections.title: Known Issues and Future Work
sections.content:
The RFC identifies several known difficulties and areas for future research. When a MOSPF router itself sends multicast datagrams, the choice of source address matters: using a serial line interface address can cause excess traffic on that link. Using any interface address as source can cause excess traffic because MOSPF always multicasts the packet back onto the source network during forwarding.

When MOSPF and non-multicast OSPF routers coexist on a LAN, a MOSPF router must be elected Designated Router, or multicast forwarding and group membership monitoring will fail on the LAN. This is an operational nuisance because OSPF's DR election algorithm is designed to minimize DR transitions, not to guarantee a particular router becomes DR. Assigning a DR Priority of 0 to all non-multicast routers works around this issue.

Future work includes analyzing multicast traffic patterns to determine if routing calculations pose undue processing burden, gaining experience with interactions between MOSPF and other multicast routing algorithms, and adding MIB support for retrieving forwarding cache entries.
sections.eli5: There are a few tricky situations: routers have to pick their source address carefully, and MOSPF routers need to be the leader on shared networks. Researchers still need to test how well MOSPF works when used with other kinds of multicast routing.
